title: Whispers from the Liminal — ep. 17 · ravensway

nodes.text: WHISPERS FROM THE LIMINAL · ep. 17 · ravensway
Ravensway. Some of you know the gallery. Fewer of you know there used to be a ride.
This came to me as three pages stapled out of order. I’ve put them back the way they wanted to go.
i.
You will want to hear the story about this one, says one friend to another.

What, about that guy only writes about other people’s nightmares.
Nah, that was some artist I know.
And you got it wrong, he was a she.

You certain?
Whatever, let’s move on.

What can you tell us about this individual?
Moves mountains by song.
That voice, and to hear it ring is to die partway.

Said can’t stay in one place for long.
So not much of a demigod then but whatever.

Mostly mortal toil so busy running up down

rung-ladder
corporate-concrete
glass-gunsteel.
Very careful breathing out braced for spine broke cracklin electric.
ii.

what are you exactly, one voice entreaties another.
staring across from whatever other self this may be
formless uncertainty a puzzle to figure
what dark secret do they dare break free

eternal gentle selfish nudgin unseats loved kin
proper positions in an ever-evolving pantheon
duck duck goose swan there and back again
kindly sit a spell by this here a-jarred window

left open by your last lover’s embrace
having formulated an all-but-certain escape plan.
weave lines through the air and connect the ...s

The quantum revolution took everyone by surprise. Some called it the return of magic, others, the singularity, and a good deal of folk correctly assumed it was the breakdown of coherent reality. Insanity for all.
Eyeing the everyday from a brand new broken perspective, as rationalizing and coherency fought their way back from the abyss. The first to return to sanity were, of course, the madmen.
Things just made sense now, or at the very least, those the longest suffering were the best equipped to deal. They quickly became the best tour guides of the new status quo.
Poets, preachers, and painter junkies, all peeking in through the fogged up window, broken prophets, all, during that brief and wondrous awful reign of chaos.

Child, where-ever is that mother of yours.
Never had one, you say? I find that hard to believe.
She has to be here someplace. Lots of Mothers in here.

Want to come inside, try to find her?
Better have something of hers to show.
In case she doesn’t recognize you.
She might remember that pretty trinket, instead.

Find the frog. He has much to show you.
I tried calling him a name, and he got mad at me.
Every day at sunset he goes and sits on the edge of the broken bridge.

The fear emitters here are some of the strongest ever recorded.
Problem was were all the other emotional pitches they used
to scale the experience. Walk in through the front door
hit you hard practically sprayed in the face with trigger data
nostalgia mixed with sadness laced with a tinge of trace panic.

Go spend a moment in the shade under the water tower
And you can practically feel the guilt, anguish and paranoia
of burying a body (alive?) right there in that loose damp earth
that clumps when rubbed together.

The experience was almost too good
such that upon leaving ravensway few ever wanted to return.
Once was enough, indeed.
The fear emitters are, I’m told, still running. Nobody pays the power bill. Goodnight.
